study: Toxicokinetics of 6:2 FTOH metabolites in pregnant and nonpregnant rats (Food Chem Toxicol 2024)
source_table: Abstract (Food Chem Toxicol 2024): 'The tss values for 5:3A in serum and tissues of adult nonpregnant animals ranged from 150 days to over a year'
notes: tss (time to steady state), NOT a half-life/clearance/Vd - recorded as reported. Range 150 d to 'over a year'; ci_high=365 is the stated lower bound of 'over a year', so the true upper end is HIGHER. 5:3A is the major metabolite of 6:2 FTOH. 4:3 FTCA flagged as an additional potentially-biopersistent metabolite. Key mechanistic result: 5:3A was NOT a substrate for renal transporters in a human kidney cell line, so renal reuptake is unlikely to explain its biopersistence. IMPORTANT for the matrix: every existing 5:3 FTCA row comes from the EPA httk package (modelled); this is an independent MEASURED in vivo source.

study: Nonlinear mixed-effects modeling of IV and oral kinetics of eleven PFAS in female mice (Environ Res 2026)
chemical: PFBA, PFHxA, GenX (HFPO-DA), PFO2OA (and 7 others: PFBS, PFOA, PFHxS, PFOS, PFDS, PFNA, PFDA)
model: nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) population TK + allometric scaling to human
source_table: Abstract (Environ Res 2026): 'Mean residence time ranged from less than 1 day for PFBA, PFHxA, GenX, and PFO2OA to up to 68 days for other PFAS'
notes: MRT, not half-life. Range is across the 11 PFAS: <1 d for PFBA/PFHxA/GenX/PFO2OA, up to 68 d for the others. RETRIEVAL GAP for the per-compound clearance table: Elsevier, not in PMC, not open access (Europe PMC inEPMC=N). Qualitative abstract findings worth noting: plasma clearance of long-chain PFCA/PFSA at least 150x lower than short-chain analogs; ether linkage cut clearance ~25-fold for GenX and ~4-fold for PFO2OA vs PFHxA; renal excretion 70-100% of total clearance for PFBS, PFBA, PFHxA, ethers, PFOA and PFDS; PFHxS and PFOS balanced renal/fecal; PFNA and PFDA primarily fecal; deep tissue compartments for PFHxA and PFO2OA prolonged terminal half-lives; PFBS showed NONLINEAR disposition. HIGHEST-VALUE remaining target for a future pass - 11 compounds x clearance/Vd/half-life, female mouse, IV+oral.

study: Early Life Uptake and Elimination of PFAS in a Seasonally Invertivorous Bird (Environ Sci Technol 2026)
n: 124 whole-blood samples from 16 sites; recaptures over 8 months at the most contaminated site
source_table: Abstract (Environ Sci Technol 2026): 'compound-specific elimination half-lives, which ranged from 29 days (PFBS) to 91 days (PFNA)'
notes: Value is an endpoint of the reported range that the abstract attributes to this specific compound. The abstract gives per-compound half-lives only for the two extremes; the other compounds' values need the full text (ACS, not open access). Juvenile sum-PFCAs and sum-PFSAs declined 0.43-1.25% per day; ADULTS showed slower elimination (not quantified in abstract). study: Transfer of selected PFAS to muscle, liver and plasma of adolescent sheep (Environ Pollut 2026)
strain_or_breed: lambs (adolescent sheep; breed not stated in abstract)
model: empirical, estimated directly from the data (apparent)
source_table: Abstract (Environ Pollut 2026): 'Apparent plasma elimination half-lives ranged from 0.3 days (PFPA) to 57 days (PFOS)'
notes: Value is an endpoint of the reported range that the abstract attributes to this specific compound. Nine PFAS were studied (PFBA, PFPA, PFHxA, PFOA, PFNA, PFDA, PFBS, PFHxS, PFOS); the abstract gives per-compound half-lives only for the two extremes, the rest need the full text (Elsevier, not open access). APPARENT half-life. Authors state this is the FIRST toxicokinetic data for PFAS other than PFOA and PFOS in male lambs. Long-chain (PFHxS, PFOS, PFNA, PFDA) accumulated more and were eliminated more slowly than short-chain. Tissue peaks: PFHxS dominant in plasma (5330 +/- 200 ug/L) and dorsal muscle (347 +/- 78 ug/kg); PFOS dominant in liver (1817 +/- 152 ug/kg). Study also reports biotransfer factors (BTF) and transfer rates (TR) not captured here. PFPA = fastest-eliminated of the nine.

study: Bioaccumulation, distribution and depuration of PFAS in chickens from a contaminated region (Chemosphere 2026)
chemical: 32 PFAS incl. PFOS (PFSA and PFCA, short- and long-chain, plus emerging PFAS)
route: environmental (reared near PFAS-contaminated industrial sites), then depuration in a PFAS-free environment
matrix: serum, breast, fat, gizzard, heart, kidney, liver, skin, thigh, eggs
source_table: Abstract (Chemosphere 2026) - depuration described qualitatively, NO half-life or rate constant reported in abstract
notes: LOGGED AS A GAP, no value claimed. Depuration over >=28 days is characterised but the abstract gives no half-life or elimination rate constant. Qualitative: concentrations up to 23x higher and a broader PFAS profile before depuration; serum, liver and kidney were the primary accumulation sites; FAT held similar levels before and after depuration (i.e. did not depurate); egg production identified as a significant elimination pathway. Full text (Elsevier, not open access) would be needed for any rate.

study: Two-Compartment PBPK with Postnatal GFR Maturation for infant blood PFAS from breast milk, Korean cohorts (Environ Sci Technol 2026)
strain_or_breed: breastfed infants, Korean birth cohorts (Cohort A n=221 in 2018; Cohort B n=204 in 2023)
model: two-compartment PBPK with postnatal glomerular filtration rate maturation function
source_table: Abstract (Environ Sci Technol 2026) - no numeric half-life or clearance reported in abstract
notes: LOGGED AS A GAP, no value claimed. The model's PK parameters (elimination half-life, GFR maturation) are not numerically reported in the abstract. Methodologically notable: global sensitivity analysis found breast-milk concentration and daily intake volume dominated output uncertainty (|PRCC| 0.82-0.91) while the PK clearance parameters had NEGLIGIBLE influence on peak concentration (|PRCC| <= 0.05) over the first six months - i.e. accumulation-dominated rather than clearance-dominated kinetics in early infancy. External benchmarking vs Fromme 2010 gave predicted/observed 0.67 and 0.61. Also reports PFHxS down 66.7% and PFNA/PFDeA up 161.5%/135.1% between 2018 and 2023 ('regrettable substitution').
